prompt:
Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create a title illustration for a children's story app, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.

FRAME (most important):
The whole wide 16:9 canvas is ONE flat sheet of warm cream cardstock (#f5efe9) with fine paper grain. A large window is cut out of it: a window cut in the silhouette of a big round porridge bowl seen from the side (a wide rounded bowl shape, flat top edge slightly arched, small foot at the bottom). It is centered horizontally, its top at about 4% of the height and its height about 74% of the canvas HEIGHT. The scene is seen THROUGH this window, built from 3 or 4 layered paper depth planes behind the sheet; the window edge shows the sheet thickness with a soft inner shadow along the top and inner edges and a light cut edge at the bottom. The lower 22% of the canvas below the window and both side areas are plain empty cream paper with nothing on them (a title is placed there later).
Around the rim of the window, a few layered paper ornaments overlap the edge at the upper-left and upper-right and one at the bottom: green oak leaves, small orange and pink paper wildflowers and one wooden spoon. Nothing else on the cream sheet.

SCENE INSIDE THE WINDOW:
Inside the cosy bear cottage in the forest: the curious golden-haired girl Goldilocks peeking happily at three bowls of porridge (big, middle, small) on a wooden table, three chairs of three sizes behind; through the round window of the cottage the three bears (papa, mama, baby) are seen walking home on a forest path. Daylight.

FACE (characters only): a simple cut-paper face — two round dot eyes, a tiny dot nose, a small curved paper-strip mouth, two round pale-pink paper cheeks. No realistic eyes, no eyelashes, no glossy highlights.

Match the characters in the reference images exactly (same faces, clothes, proportions). Characters may slightly overlap the lower rim of the window.

LIGHTING:
Use soft, diffuse studio-style lighting from the upper-left, mainly to reveal the edges and spacing of stacked paper layers.
Shadows should be short, soft, restrained, and consistent.
They must feel like paper-layer shadows, NOT realistic sunlight shadows cast by natural three-dimensional objects.

OVERALL FEELING:
Warm, tactile, whimsical, handcrafted, elegant, slightly imperfect, sophisticated paper craft, photographed straight from the front.

NO text.
NO photorealism.
NO glossy surfaces.
NO realistic 3D modeling.
NO inflated or rounded forms.
NO clay-like volume.
NO gradients.
NO painterly rendering.
NO airbrushed shading.
NO realistic sunlight shadows.
NO deep ambient occlusion.
NO thick beveled edges.
NO plastic appearance.
NO felt or fabric appearance.
NO fur-fibre texture.
NO title, NO letters anywhere.

Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create ONE character or object sprite, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art: a figure assembled from individually cut pieces of matte colored cardstock and fine-grain craft paper.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.
